World Day for Grandparents and the Elderly is celebrated today , 26 July, Feast of Sts
Joachim and Anne , parents of Mary and grandparents of Jesus .
We thank God for the gift of grandparents and the elderly in our lives and, especially, for the
wisdom, love and faith passed down through generations in our families and in our parishes.
The theme for the 202 6 celebration is ‘I will never forget you ’ (Isaiah 49:15). In his Message
for the Day, Pope Leo asks that we “revive the beautiful custom of visiting grandparents, the
elderly members of the family and those who have no one to visit them …..Ensure that the words
of the prophet, ‘But I will never forget you ’ take the form of a tender and affectionate encounter. ”
We pray for the intentions of all grandparents and the elderly :
Sts Joachim and Anne, pray for all. Aghyaran

Parish Youth Group
We are hoping to launch a new Parish Youth Group for young people in Years 8–10 from September and
we are looking for enthusiastic adult volunteers. The youth group will meet once per month in the crypt
on Saturdays from 4:30pm , followed by the Vigil Mass at 6:30pm. This is a wonderful opportunity to
support our young people in their faith journey, build community, and have a positive impact in the parish.
We are seeking volunteers who can:
Help supervise and support activities
Assist with organising sessions and events
Encourage and accompany young people in a welcoming, safe environment
No previous experience is necessary —just a willingness to help and a friendly, supportive attitude.
Training and safeguarding guidance will be provided as required.
If you feel called to be part of this important opportunity for our youth,
please contact Caroline McAfee
by emailing
ckellyd@hotmail.com
, or call 07517391743.

Parish Bulletin
for
Ramoan
(Ballycastle, Glenshesk & Rathlin)
and
Ballintoy & Ballinlea
(Mass Readings: Sunday Cycle A)
Exposition of the Blessed Sacrament
every Monday, immediately after 10am Mass until 1.30pm. All welcome Upcoming Mass Schedule
Glenshesk : Sun 12th July at 9am. Ballinlea : Sun 19th July at 9am. Ballintoy : Sat 1st August at 5.30pm Mass and Confessions Schedule in Ballycastle
Vigil Mass on Saturday at 6.30pm, and Masses on Sunday at 10am and 12noon.
Daily Mass:10am, with Sacrament of Reconciliation after Saturday 10am Mass
Parish Youth Group
We are hoping to launch a new Parish Youth Group for young people in Years 8–10 from September and
we are looking for enthusiastic adult volunteers. The youth group will meet once per month in the crypt
on Saturdays from 4:30pm , followed by the Vigil Mass at 6:30pm. This is a wonderful opportunity to
support our young people in their faith journey, build community, and have a positive impact in the parish.
We are seeking volunteers who can:
Help supervise and support activities
Assist with organising sessions and events
Encourage and accompany young people in a welcoming, safe environment
No previous experience is necessary —just a willingness to help and a friendly, supportive attitude.
Training and safeguarding guidance will be provided as required.
If you feel called to be part of this important opportunity for our youth,
please contact Caroline McAfee
by emailing
ckellyd@hotmail.com
, or call 07517391743.
Words of Spirit and LIife
An evening with Jeff Cavins
Sunday 26th July 2026, 7pm Voco Hotel Belfast.
Spend an inspiring evening with Jeff Cavins, the internationally renowned Bible teacher, author, and
creator of The Great Adventure Bible Timeline that shaped the hugely popular Bible in a Year podcast ,
meeting others who love the Word, sharing in a time of prayer led by Fr Conor McGrath,
and being reminded that the words of Jesus are Spirit and they are Life.

Parish Youth Group

we are looking for enthusiastic adult volunteers. The youth group will meet once per month in the crypt
on Saturdays from 4:30pm , followed by the Vigil Mass at 6:30pm. This is a wonderful opportunity to
support our young people in their faith journey, build community, and have a positive impact in the parish.
We are seeking volunteers who can:
Help supervise and support activities
Assist with organising sessions and events
Encourage and accompany young people in a welcoming, safe environment
No previous experience is necessary —just a willingness to help and a friendly, supportive attitude.

by emailing
ckellyd@hotmail.com
, or call 07517391743.

Exposition of the Blessed Sacrament
every Monday, immediately after 10am Mass until 1.30pm. All welcome Upcoming Mass Schedule
Glenshesk : Sun 12th July at 9am. Ballinlea : Sun 19th July at 9am. Ballintoy : Sat 1st August at 5.30pm Mass and Confessions Schedule in Ballycastle
Vigil Mass on Saturday at 6.30pm, and Masses on Sunday at 10am and 12noon.
Daily Mass:10am, with Sacrament of Reconciliation after Saturday 10am Mass
Parish Youth Group
We are hoping to launch a new Parish Youth Group for young people in Years 8–10 from September and
we are looking for enthusiastic adult volunteers. The youth group will meet once per month in the crypt
on Saturdays from 4:30pm , followed by the Vigil Mass at 6:30pm. This is a wonderful opportunity to
support our young people in their faith journey, build community, and have a positive impact in the parish.
We are seeking volunteers who can:
Help supervise and support activities
Assist with organising sessions and events
Encourage and accompany young people in a welcoming, safe environment
No previous experience is necessary —just a willingness to help and a friendly, supportive attitude.
Training and safeguarding guidance will be provided as required.
If you feel called to be part of this important opportunity for our youth,
please contact Caroline McAfee
by emailing
ckellyd@hotmail.com
, or call 07517391743.

An evening with Jeff Cavins

creator of The Great Adventure Bible Timeline that shaped the hugely popular Bible in a Year podcast ,
meeting others who love the Word, sharing in a time of prayer led by Fr Conor McGrath,
and being reminded that the words of Jesus are Spirit and they are Life.

Parish Youth Group

we are looking for enthusiastic adult volunteers. The youth group will meet once per month in the crypt
on Saturdays from 4:30pm , followed by the Vigil Mass at 6:30pm. This is a wonderful opportunity to
support our young people in their faith journey, build community, and have a positive impact in the parish.
We are seeking volunteers who can:
Help supervise and support activities
Assist with organising sessions and events
Encourage and accompany young people in a welcoming, safe environment
No previous experience is necessary —just a willingness to help and a friendly, supportive attitude.

We are seeking volunteers who can:
Help supervise and support activities
Assist with organising sessions and events
Encourage and accompany young people in a welcoming, safe environment

Follow in Love
The first big moment of vocation is baptism. The anointing of chrism at baptism might be called the anointing for vocation. The baptismal vocation is for witness, love and service. This is expressed in ways in which people live out their baptism in married life, single life - and within the single life, maybe religious life or priesthood.
Our active witness is to the life and the values of Jesus in our lives. Teaching is not itself a vocation, for example, but the way we teach is a way of living out our vocation. It is the same with many of the helping professions and employments. Being a good neighbour can be a living out of our vocation.
We witness to love in marriage, in family, extended family, and in friendship. Any love is a sharing in the love of God. In the moments of unselfish love in any relationship, we are living out our vocation. When we love, we are doing God's will!
We witness to service in the wider world in our care for the poor and in welcoming the stranger: the widow, the orphan, the immigrant - in fact anybody needy.

The first big moment of vocation is baptism. The anointing of chrism at baptism might be called the anointing for vocation. The baptismal vocation is for witness, love and service. This is expressed in ways in which people live out their baptism in married life, single life - and within the single life, maybe religious life or priesthood.
Our active witness is to the life and the values of Jesus in our lives. Teaching is not itself a vocation, for example, but the way we teach is a way of living out our vocation. It is the same with many of the helping professions and employments. Being a good neighbour can be a living out of our vocation.
We witness to love in marriage, in family, extended family, and in friendship. Any love is a sharing in the love of God. In the moments of unselfish love in any relationship, we are living out our vocation. When we love, we are doing God's will!
We witness to service in the wider world in our care for the poor and in welcoming the stranger: the widow, the orphan, the immigrant - in fact anybody needy.

Follow in Love
The first big moment of vocation is baptism. The anointing of chrism at baptism might be called the anointing for vocation. The baptismal vocation is for witness, love and service. This is expressed in ways in which people live out their baptism in married life, single life - and within the single life, maybe religious life or priesthood.
Our active witness is to the life and the values of Jesus in our lives. Teaching is not itself a vocation, for example, but the way we teach is a way of living out our vocation. It is the same with many of the helping professions and employments. Being a good neighbour can be a living out of our vocation.
We witness to love in marriage, in family, extended family, and in friendship. Any love is a sharing in the love of God. In the moments of unselfish love in any relationship, we are living out our vocation. When we love, we are doing God's will!
We witness to service in the wider world in our care for the poor and in welcoming the stranger: the widow, the orphan, the immigrant - in fact anybody needy.

MINISTRY OF WELCOME
Booking Masses, Baptisms and Weddings
Masses can be booked in the sacristy well in advance to ensure your preferred dates are available.
Baptisms: At least one month’s notice is required. To book a baptism parents/guardians must present the child’s long birth certificate, complete the baptism request form, meet with one of our baptism team and attend weekly Mass during the month prior to the date of the Baptism. If parents cannot commit to the preparation, the Baptism will be rebooked to a later date.
Weddings must be booked by the couple themselves. Couples are required to give at least six months’ notice of marriage to ensure the preferred date is available and that there is adequate time to complete all Civil and Church paperwork.

MINISTRY OF WELCOME
Booking Masses, Baptisms and Weddings
Masses can be booked in the sacristy well in advance to ensure your preferred dates are available.
Baptisms: At least one month’s notice is required. To book a baptism parents/guardians must present the child’s long birth certificate, complete the baptism request form, meet with one of our baptism team and attend weekly Mass during the month prior to the date of the Baptism. If parents cannot commit to the preparation, the Baptism will be rebooked to a later date.
Weddings must be booked by the couple themselves. Couples are required to give at least six months’ notice of marriage to ensure the preferred date is available and that there is adequate time to complete all Civil and Church paperwork.

PARISH DRAW

DAY FOR LIFE
Jesus sanctified the beginning of life as an unborn child, hidden in the womb of Our Lady. Mary knew she was carrying the Son of God – God and man – as soon as He was conceived. John the Baptist leapt in his mother Elizabeth’s womb when Mary greeted her. Our Lady treasured Our Lord in her heart and womb until His birth. To read the full bishops’ message visit
www.councilforlife.ie
FATHERS' DAY
If there’s no self-sacrifice, it’s not fatherhood! Fathers are givers.
FATHERS' DAY PRAYER
God our Father, we give You thanks and praise for fathers, young and old. May they find courage and perseverance in their vocation. May their lives follow the example of Saint Joseph, model in the protection and care of the family. We remember fathers, grandfathers and great-grandfathers who are no longer with us, but who guided us in the Faith, nourished us with their love and live forever in our memory. Through the prayers of St Joseph, may our fathers receive abundant blessings today.
40 HOURS ADORATION
Friday to Sunday, 3rd-5th July, Oratory. Please sign up!
NOVENA TO ST OLIVER PLUNKETT
22nd - 30th June – Glorious Martyr, Saint Oliver, who willingly gave your life for your faith, helps us to be strong in faith. May we be loyal like you to the See of Peter. By your intercession and example, may all hatred and bitterness be banished from the hearts of Irish men and women. May the peace of Christ reign in our hearts, as it did in your heart, even at the moment of your death. Pause for your own intentions.
St Oliver Plunkett, pray for us and for Ireland.
CHURCH SIGN
Trouble sleeping? We have sermons. Come and hear one!

May their lives follow the example of Saint Joseph, model in the protection and care of the family. We remember fathers, grandfathers and great-grandfathers who are no longer with us, but who guided us in the Faith, nourished us with their love and live forever in our memory. Through the prayers of St Joseph, may our fathers receive abundant blessings today.
40 HOURS ADORATION
Friday to Sunday, 3rd-5th July, Oratory. Please sign up!
NOVENA TO ST OLIVER PLUNKETT
22nd - 30th June – Glorious Martyr, Saint Oliver, who willingly gave your life for your faith, helps us to be strong in faith. May we be loyal like you to the See of Peter. By your intercession and example, may all hatred and bitterness be banished from the hearts of Irish men and women. May the peace of Christ reign in our hearts, as it did in your heart, even at the moment of your death. Pause for your own intentions.
St Oliver Plunkett, pray for us and for Ireland.
CHURCH SIGN
Trouble sleeping? We have sermons. Come and hear one!

May their lives follow the example of Saint Joseph, model in the protection and care of the family. We remember fathers, grandfathers and great-grandfathers who are no longer with us, but who guided us in the Faith, nourished us with their love and live forever in our memory. Through the prayers of St Joseph, may our fathers receive abundant blessings today.
40 HOURS ADORATION
Friday to Sunday, 3rd-5th July, Oratory. Please sign up!
NOVENA TO ST OLIVER PLUNKETT
22nd - 30th June – Glorious Martyr, Saint Oliver, who willingly gave your life for your faith, helps us to be strong in faith. May we be loyal like you to the See of Peter. By your intercession and example, may all hatred and bitterness be banished from the hearts of Irish men and women. May the peace of Christ reign in our hearts, as it did in your heart, even at the moment of your death. Pause for your own intentions.
St Oliver Plunkett, pray for us and for Ireland.
CHURCH SIGN
Trouble sleeping? We have sermons. Come and hear one!

COLLECTION
COLLECTION
€688. Restoration: €512. Donations: €200, £40, €30, €20. Merci!
PARISH DRAW
- Wednesday 25th June, Hall, 9pm. Make sure you have paid in!
DAY FOR LIFE
- Jesus sanctified the beginning of life as an unborn child, hidden in the womb of Our Lady. Mary knew she was carrying the Son of God – God and man – as soon as He was conceived. John the Baptist leapt in his mother Elizabeth's womb when Mary greeted her. Our Lady treasured Our Lord in her heart and womb until His birth. To read the full bishops' message visit
www.councilforlife.ie
FATHERS’ DAY
- If there’s no self-sacrifice, it’s not fatherhood! Fathers are givers.
FATHERS’ DAY PRAYER
- God our Father, we give You thanks and praise for fathers, young and old. May they find courage and perseverance in their vocation. May their lives follow the example of Saint Joseph, model in the protection and care of the family. We remember fathers, grandfathers and great-grandfathers who are no longer with us, but who guided us in the Faith, nourished us with their love and live forever in our memory. Through the prayers of St Joseph, may our fathers receive abundant blessings today.
40 HOURS ADORATION
- Friday to Sunday, 3rd-5th July, Oratory. Please sign up!
NOVENA TO ST OLIVER PLUNKETT
- 22nd - 30th June – Glorious Martyr, Saint Oliver, who willingly gave your life for your faith, helps us to be strong in faith. May we be loyal like you to the See of Peter. By your intercession and example, may all hatred and bitterness be banished from the hearts of Irish men and women. May the peace of Christ reign in our hearts, as it did in your heart, even at the moment of your death. Pause for your own intentions. St Oliver Plunkett, pray for us and for Ireland.
CHURCH SIGN
- Trouble sleeping? We have sermons. Come and hear one!

PARISH DRAW
- Wednesday 25th June, Hall, 9pm. Make sure you have paid in!
DAY FOR LIFE
- Jesus sanctified the beginning of life as an unborn child, hidden in the womb of Our Lady. Mary knew she was carrying the Son of God – God and man – as soon as He was conceived. John the Baptist leapt in his mother Elizabeth's womb when Mary greeted her. Our Lady treasured Our Lord in her heart and womb until His birth. To read the full bishops' message visit
www.councilforlife.ie
FATHERS’ DAY
- If there’s no self-sacrifice, it’s not fatherhood! Fathers are givers.
FATHERS’ DAY PRAYER
- God our Father, we give You thanks and praise for fathers, young and old. May they find courage and perseverance in their vocation. May their lives follow the example of Saint Joseph, model in the protection and care of the family. We remember fathers, grandfathers and great-grandfathers who are no longer with us, but who guided us in the Faith, nourished us with their love and live forever in our memory. Through the prayers of St Joseph, may our fathers receive abundant blessings today.
40 HOURS ADORATION
- Friday to Sunday, 3rd-5th July, Oratory. Please sign up!
NOVENA TO ST OLIVER PLUNKETT
- 22nd - 30th June – Glorious Martyr, Saint Oliver, who willingly gave your life for your faith, helps us to be strong in faith. May we be loyal like you to the See of Peter. By your intercession and example, may all hatred and bitterness be banished from the hearts of Irish men and women. May the peace of Christ reign in our hearts, as it did in your heart, even at the moment of your death. Pause for your own intentions. St Oliver Plunkett, pray for us and for Ireland.

- Trouble sleeping? We have sermons. Come and hear one!

€688. Restoration: €512. Donations: €200, £40, €30, €20. Merci!
PARISH DRAW
- Wednesday 25th June, Hall, 9pm. Make sure you have paid in!
DAY FOR LIFE
- Jesus sanctified the beginning of life as an unborn child, hidden in the womb of Our Lady. Mary knew she was carrying the Son of God – God and man – as soon as He was conceived. John the Baptist leapt in his mother Elizabeth's womb when Mary greeted her. Our Lady treasured Our Lord in her heart and womb until His birth. To read the full bishops' message visit
www.councilforlife.ie
FATHERS’ DAY
- If there’s no self-sacrifice, it’s not fatherhood! Fathers are givers.
FATHERS’ DAY PRAYER
- God our Father, we give You thanks and praise for fathers, young and old. May they find courage and perseverance in their vocation. May their lives follow the example of Saint Joseph, model in the protection and care of the family. We remember fathers, grandfathers and great-grandfathers who are no longer with us, but who guided us in the Faith, nourished us with their love and live forever in our memory. Through the prayers of St Joseph, may our fathers receive abundant blessings today.
40 HOURS ADORATION
- Friday to Sunday, 3rd-5th July, Oratory. Please sign up!
NOVENA TO ST OLIVER PLUNKETT
- 22nd - 30th June – Glorious Martyr, Saint Oliver, who willingly gave your life for your faith, helps us to be strong in faith. May we be loyal like you to the See of Peter. By your intercession and example, may all hatred and bitterness be banished from the hearts of Irish men and women. May the peace of Christ reign in our hearts, as it did in your heart, even at the moment of your death. Pause for your own intentions. St Oliver Plunkett, pray for us and for Ireland.
CHURCH SIGN
- Trouble sleeping? We have sermons. Come and hear one!

COLLECTION – £688. Restoration: £512. Donations: £200, £40, £30, £20 . Merci!
PARISH DRA W – Wednesday 25th June, Hall, 9pm. Make sure you have paid in!
DAY FOR LIFE – Jesus sanctified the beginning of life as an unborn child, hidden in the womb of Our Lady . Mary
knew she was carrying the Son of God – God and man – as soon as He was conceived. John the Baptist leapt in
his mother Elizabeth’ s womb when Mary greeted her . Our Lady treasured Our Lord in her heart and womb until His
birth. T o read the full bishops’ message visit www .councilforlife.ie
FATHERS’ DAY – If there’ s no self-sacrifice, it’ s not fatherhood! Fathers are givers.
FATHERS’ DAY PRA YER – God our Father , we give You thanks and praise for fathers, young and old. May they
find courage and perseverance in their vocation. May their lives follow the example of Saint Joseph, model in the
protection and care of the family . We remember fathers, grandfathers and great-grandfathers who are no longer with
us, but who guided us in the Faith, nourished us with their love and live forever in our memory . Through the prayers
of St Joseph, may our fathers receive abundant blessings today .
40 HOURS ADORA TION – Friday to Sunday , 3rd-5th July, Oratory . Please sign up!
NOVENA TO ST OLIVER PLUNKETT – 22nd - 30th June – Glorious Martyr , Saint Oliver , who willingly gave your life
for your faith, help us to be strong in faith. May we be loyal like you to the See of Peter . By your intercession and
example, may all hatred and bitterness be banished from the hearts of Irish men and women. May the peace of
Christ reign in our hearts, as it did in your heart, even at the moment of your death. Pause for your own intentions.
St Oliver Plunkett, pray for us and for Ireland.

knew she was carrying the Son of God – God and man – as soon as He was conceived. John the Baptist leapt in
his mother Elizabeth’ s womb when Mary greeted her . Our Lady treasured Our Lord in her heart and womb until His
birth. T o read the full bishops’ message visit www .councilforlife.ie
FATHERS’ DAY – If there’ s no self-sacrifice, it’ s not fatherhood! Fathers are givers.
FATHERS’ DAY PRA YER – God our Father , we give You thanks and praise for fathers, young and old. May they
find courage and perseverance in their vocation. May their lives follow the example of Saint Joseph, model in the
protection and care of the family . We remember fathers, grandfathers and great-grandfathers who are no longer with
us, but who guided us in the Faith, nourished us with their love and live forever in our memory . Through the prayers
of St Joseph, may our fathers receive abundant blessings today .
40 HOURS ADORA TION – Friday to Sunday , 3rd-5th July, Oratory . Please sign up!
NOVENA TO ST OLIVER PLUNKETT – 22nd - 30th June – Glorious Martyr , Saint Oliver , who willingly gave your life
for your faith, help us to be strong in faith. May we be loyal like you to the See of Peter . By your intercession and
example, may all hatred and bitterness be banished from the hearts of Irish men and women. May the peace of
Christ reign in our hearts, as it did in your heart, even at the moment of your death. Pause for your own intentions.
St Oliver Plunkett, pray for us and for Ireland.

his mother Elizabeth’ s womb when Mary greeted her . Our Lady treasured Our Lord in her heart and womb until His
birth. T o read the full bishops’ message visit www .councilforlife.ie
FATHERS’ DAY – If there’ s no self-sacrifice, it’ s not fatherhood! Fathers are givers.
FATHERS’ DAY PRA YER – God our Father , we give You thanks and praise for fathers, young and old. May they
find courage and perseverance in their vocation. May their lives follow the example of Saint Joseph, model in the
protection and care of the family . We remember fathers, grandfathers and great-grandfathers who are no longer with
us, but who guided us in the Faith, nourished us with their love and live forever in our memory . Through the prayers
of St Joseph, may our fathers receive abundant blessings today .
40 HOURS ADORA TION – Friday to Sunday , 3rd-5th July, Oratory . Please sign up!
NOVENA TO ST OLIVER PLUNKETT – 22nd - 30th June – Glorious Martyr , Saint Oliver , who willingly gave your life
for your faith, help us to be strong in faith. May we be loyal like you to the See of Peter . By your intercession and
example, may all hatred and bitterness be banished from the hearts of Irish men and women. May the peace of
Christ reign in our hearts, as it did in your heart, even at the moment of your death. Pause for your own intentions.
St Oliver Plunkett, pray for us and for Ireland.

Knock Pilgrimage to Pray for Peace in the Holy Land: People from all over Ireland are invited to Knock Shrine on Saturday 16th May for a special pilgrimage to pray for peace in the Holy Land. www.acnireland.org

Vocations Prayer: In our first reading this weekend we hear about the people of Samaria receiving the Holy Spirit. As we approach Pentecost, we pray for a fresh and powerful outpouring of the Holy Spirit on the Church, on the world, on our country, on our parish communities, and on each one of us. May the Spirit fill the hearts and minds of deacons, seminarians, and all those discerning a vocation to the diocesan priesthood, and may many more hear and follow the call to serve the Church as priests. The Little Way Novena in St. Eugene’s Cathedral – 9th – 17th May: The theme is ‘My Peace Consists in Remaining Little’. The Novena begins at the 7.30pm Mass on Saturday 9th May with the Sacrament of the Sick. Devotions and talk on Sunday 10th May at 6.00pm. Monday to Friday (11th – 15th May) Novena Masses at 6.30am and 10.00am each morning and an evening service with a guest speaker at 7.30 pm. Saturday 16th May 10.00am Mass for those who have died. The Novena closes with blessing of the roses on Sunday 17th May at 3.00pm. Everyone is welcome at St. Eugene’s Cathedral for this time of prayer and petition. Knock Pilgrimage to Pray for Peace in the Holy Land: People from all over Ireland are invited to Knock Shrine on Saturday 16th May for a special pilgrimage to pray for peace in the Holy Land. The pilgrimage, organised by the papal charity Aid to the Church in Need, will be led by Bishop William Shomali from Bethlehem. Bishop Shomali will offer a message of hope at 11.00am and celebrate Mass at 3.00pm. All are welcome. More information at
www.acnireland.org

May the Spirit fill the hearts and minds of deacons, seminarians, and all those discerning a vocation to the diocesan priesthood, and may many more hear and follow the call to serve the Church as priests. The Little Way Novena in St. Eugene’s Cathedral – 9th – 17th May: The theme is ‘My Peace Consists in Remaining Little’. The Novena begins at the 7.30pm Mass on Saturday 9th May with the Sacrament of the Sick. Devotions and talk on Sunday 10th May at 6.00pm. Monday to Friday (11th – 15th May) Novena Masses at 6.30am and 10.00am each morning and an evening service with a guest speaker at 7.30 pm. Saturday 16th May 10.00am Mass for those who have died. The Novena closes with blessing of the roses on Sunday 17th May at 3.00pm. Everyone is welcome at St. Eugene’s Cathedral for this time of prayer and petition. Knock Pilgrimage to Pray for Peace in the Holy Land: People from all over Ireland are invited to Knock Shrine on Saturday 16th May for a special pilgrimage to pray for peace in the Holy Land. The pilgrimage, organised by the papal charity Aid to the Church in Need, will be led by Bishop William Shomali from Bethlehem. Bishop Shomali will offer a message of hope at 11.00am and celebrate Mass at 3.00pm. All are welcome. More information at
www.acnireland.org

Vocations Prayer:
In our first reading this weekend we hear about the people of Samaria receiving the Holy Spirit. As we approach Pentecost, we pray for a fresh and powerful outpouring of the Holy Spirit on the Church, on the world, on our country, on our parish communities, and on each one of us. May the Spirit fill the hearts and minds of deacons, seminarians, and all those discerning a vocation to the diocesan priesthood, and may many more hear and follow the call to serve the Church as priests.
The Little Way Novena in St. Eugene's Cathedral – 9th – 17th May:
The theme is 'My Peace Consists in Remaining Little'. The Novena begins at the 7.30pm Mass on Saturday 9th May with the Sacrament of the Sick. Devotions and talk on Sunday 10th May at 6.00pm. Monday to Friday (11th – 15th May) Novena Masses at 6.30am and 10.00am each morning and an evening service with a guest speaker at 7.30 pm. Saturday 16th May 10.00am Mass for those who have died. The Novena closes with blessing of the roses on Sunday 17th May at 3.00pm. Everyone is welcome at St. Eugene's Cathedral for this time of prayer and petition.

The Forty Hours Devotions † Exposition of the Blessed Sacrament takes place this weekend, Sunday 10th to Monday 11th May in St. Mary's, Altinure from 10.30am to 6.00pm on Sunday and Monday. Exposition will begin after the Sunday morning 10.30am Mass concluding with Devotions and Benediction at 6.00pm that evening. It will resume after 10.00am Mass on Monday morning with the 40 Hours ending at 6.00pm with Devotions and Benediction that evening. Everyone is welcome to visit the church or go online and spend a short while in prayer before the Blessed Sacrament.
A Month's Mind Mass for the happy repose of the soul of Anne O'Neill, RIP, will be celebrated on Saturday 16th May in St. Joseph's Church, Fincairn at 7.00pm.
Visitation of the Sick &amp; Housebound will take place on the following days this week: Wednesday 13th May - Foreglen and Carnanbane. Thursday 14th May - Park. Friday 15th May - Feeny. Please let Fr. Dermot know if you would not like a visit by contacting the Parochial House on
028 777 81223
.
The local All Ireland Rosary Rally will be held in Market Street, Limavady at 3.00pm on Saturday 16th May. All welcome. Volunteers needed to help with banners, and distributing materials. Thank you in advance. More details on 077 3033 0028.
Annual Parish Car Wash for HOPE Camp 2026
The Annual Parish Car wash will take place on Sunday 17th May from 8.30am to 1.30pm - Gate closes at 1.00pm.
All proceeds from this year's car wash will go towards activities planned for the children of the parish at this summer's HOPE Camp.
Thank you in advance - Your support is greatly appreciated.
Vocations Prayer:
In our first reading this weekend we hear about the people of Samaria receiving the Holy Spirit. As we approach Pentecost, we pray for a fresh and powerful outpouring of the Holy Spirit on the Church, on the world, on our country, on our parish communities, and on each one of us. May the Spirit fill the hearts and minds of deacons, seminarians, and all those discerning a vocation to the diocesan priesthood, and may many more hear and follow the call to serve the Church as priests.
The Little Way Novena in St. Eugene's Cathedral – 9th – 17th May:
The theme is 'My Peace Consists in Remaining Little'. The Novena begins at the 7.30pm Mass on Saturday 9th May with the Sacrament of the Sick. Devotions and talk on Sunday 10th May at 6.00pm. Monday to Friday (11th – 15th May) Novena Masses at 6.30am and 10.00am each morning and an evening service with a guest speaker at 7.30 pm. Saturday 16th May 10.00am Mass for those who have died. The Novena closes with blessing of the roses on Sunday 17th May at 3.00pm. Everyone is welcome at St. Eugene's Cathedral for this time of prayer and petition.
Knock Pilgrimage to Pray for Peace in the Holy Land:
People from all over Ireland are invited to Knock Shrine on Saturday 16th May for a special pilgrimage to pray for peace in the Holy Land. The pilgrimage, organised by the papal charity Aid to the Church in Need, will be led by Bishop William Shomali from Bethle

May the Spirit fill the hearts and minds of deacons, seminarians, and all those discerning a vocation to the diocesan priesthood, and may many more hear and follow the call to serve the Church as priests.
The Little Way Novena in St. Eugene's Cathedral – 9th – 17th May:
The theme is 'My Peace Consists in Remaining Little'. The Novena begins at the 7.30pm Mass on Saturday 9th May with the Sacrament of the Sick. Devotions and talk on Sunday 10th May at 6.00pm. Monday to Friday (11th – 15th May) Novena Masses at 6.30am and 10.00am each morning and an evening service with a guest speaker at 7.30 pm. Saturday 16th May 10.00am Mass for those who have died. The Novena closes with blessing of the roses on Sunday 17th May at 3.00pm. Everyone is welcome at St. Eugene's Cathedral for this time of prayer and petition.
Knock Pilgrimage to Pray for Peace in the Holy Land:
People from all over Ireland are invited to Knock Shrine on Saturday 16th May for a special pilgrimage to pray for peace in the Holy Land. The pilgrimage, organised by the papal charity Aid to the Church in Need, will be led by Bishop William Shomali from Bethle

The Forty Hours Devotions † Exposition of the Blessed Sacrament takes place this weekend, Sunday 10th to Monday 11th May in St. Mary's, Altinure from 10.30am to 6.00pm on Sunday and Monday. Annual Parish Car Wash for HOPE Camp 2026

Thank you in advance - Your support is greatly appreciated.
Vocations Prayer:
In our first reading this weekend we hear about the people of Samaria receiving the Holy Spirit. As we approach Pentecost, we pray for a fresh and powerful outpouring of the Holy Spirit on the Church, on the world, on our country, on our parish communities, and on each one of us. May the Spirit fill the hearts and minds of deacons, seminarians, and all those discerning a vocation to the diocesan priesthood, and may many more hear and follow the call to serve the Church as priests.
The Little Way Novena in St. Eugene's Cathedral – 9th – 17th May:
The theme is 'My Peace Consists in Remaining Little'. The Novena begins at the 7.30pm Mass on Saturday 9th May with the Sacrament of the Sick. Devotions and talk on Sunday 10th May at 6.00pm. Monday to Friday (11th – 15th May) Novena Masses at 6.30am and 10.00am each morning and an evening service with a guest speaker at 7.30 pm. Saturday 16th May 10.00am Mass for those who have died. The Novena closes with blessing of the roses on Sunday 17th May at 3.00pm. Everyone is welcome at St. Eugene's Cathedral for this time of prayer and petition.

May the Spirit fill the hearts and minds of deacons, seminarians, and all those discerning a vocation to the diocesan priesthood, and may many more hear and follow the call to serve the Church as priests.
The Little Way Novena in St. Eugene's Cathedral – 9th – 17th May:
The theme is 'My Peace Consists in Remaining Little'. The Novena begins at the 7.30pm Mass on Saturday 9th May with the Sacrament of the Sick. Devotions and talk on Sunday 10th May at 6.00pm. Monday to Friday (11th – 15th May) Novena Masses at 6.30am and 10.00am each morning and an evening service with a guest speaker at 7.30 pm. Saturday 16th May 10.00am Mass for those who have died. The Novena closes with blessing of the roses on Sunday 17th May at 3.00pm. Everyone is welcome at St. Eugene's Cathedral for this time of prayer and petition.
Knock Pilgrimage to Pray for Peace in the Holy Land:
People from all over Ireland are invited to Knock Shrine on Saturday 16th May for a special pilgrimage to pray for peace in the Holy Land. The pilgrimage, organised by the papal charity Aid to the Church in Need, will be led by Bishop William Shomali from Bethle

Booking Masses, Baptisms and Weddings
Masses can be booked in the sacristy well in advance to ensure your preferred dates are available.
Baptisms At least one month's notice is required. To book a baptism parents/guardians must present the child's long birth certificate, complete the baptism request form, meet with one of our Baptism team and attend weekly Mass during the month prior to the date of the Baptism. If parents cannot commit to the preparation, the Baptism will be rebooked to a later date.
Weddings must be booked by the couple themselves. Couples are required to give at least six months' notice of marriage to ensure the preferred date is available and that there is adequate time to complete all Civil and Church paperwork.

Booking Masses, Baptisms and Weddings
Masses can be booked in the sacristy well in advance to ensure your preferred dates are available.
Baptisms At least one month's notice is required. To book a baptism parents/guardians must present the child's long birth certificate, complete the baptism request form, meet with one of our Baptism team and attend weekly Mass during the month prior to the date of the Baptism. If parents cannot commit to the preparation, the Baptism will be rebooked to a later date.
Weddings must be booked by the couple themselves. Couples are required to give at least six months' notice of marriage to ensure the preferred date is available and that there is adequate time to complete all Civil and Church paperwork.

**Booking Masses, Baptisms and Weddings**
Masses can be booked in the sacristy well in advance to ensure your preferred dates are available.
Baptisms At least one month's notice is required. To book a baptism parents/guardians must present the child's long birth certificate, complete the baptism request form, meet with one of our Baptism team and attend weekly Mass during the month prior to the date of the Baptism. If parents cannot commit to the preparation, the Baptism will be rebooked to a later date.
Weddings must be booked by the couple themselves. Couples are required to give at least six months' notice of marriage to ensure the preferred date is available and that there is adequate time to complete all Civil and Church paperwork.

**Booking Masses, Baptisms and Weddings**
Masses can be booked in the sacristy well in advance to ensure your preferred dates are available.
Baptisms At least one month's notice is required. To book a baptism parents/guardians must present the child's long birth certificate, complete the baptism request form, meet with one of our Baptism team and attend weekly Mass during the month prior to the date of the Baptism. If parents cannot commit to the preparation, the Baptism will be rebooked to a later date.
Weddings must be booked by the couple themselves. Couples are required to give at least six months' notice of marriage to ensure the preferred date is available and that there is adequate time to complete all Civil and Church paperwork.
